Thyroxine  or T4 is one of two major hormones derived from the thyroid gland; the other being triiodothyronine (T3). The major form of thyroid hormone in the blood is thyroxine (T4); which has a longer half-life than T3. In humans; the ratio of T4 to T3 released into the blood is approximately 14:1.
